Label: Claim ID
Definition: A unique identifier for one Claim record, meaning one atomic claim as reported by one publication. Generated by the registry at claim registration.

Label: ClaimsDB Metadata
Definition: Root grouping property for all ClaimsDB metadata: registry, bibliographic, study, claim record, SciScore and extraction provenance. General extraction instructions that apply to every extracted field are attached to this property.

Label: Bibliographic Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the bibliographic identity of a publication: title, authors, date, venue and links.

Label: Article Title
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The title of the article. Taken from a bibliographic lookup; extracted by the LLM only as a fallback.

Label: Listed Authors
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The authors of the article as listed. Taken from a bibliographic lookup; extracted by the LLM only as a fallback.

Label: Publication Date
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The date the article was published.

Label: Publication Year
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The year the article was published, derived from the publication date.

Label: Publication Link
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: A link to the article.

Label: DOI Link
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The DOI link of the article.

Label: PubMed Central Link
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The PubMed Central link of the article, where one exists.

Label: PubMed Link
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The PubMed link of the article.

Label: Publication Venue
Filled_By: Bibliographic lookup (Crossref, PubMed, PMC XML); LLM only as fallback
Definition: The journal or other venue in which the article was published.

Label: Claim Record Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for everything recorded about one Claim record. Fields are extracted from the article by the claims call, except the registration fields, which scripts derive afterwards.

Label: Claim Context Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the paper-specific context of a claim that is displayed to experts for comparison: the population the claim applies to and its statistics.
Standards_And_Sources: Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Age Group
Allowed_Values: Child; Adolescent; Adult; Older Adult; Mixed; Not Specified
Definition: The age group of the participants to which the claim applies. It is a coarse facet used to show whether claims about the same finding come from comparable ages.

Label: Claim Age Range
Definition: The age of the participants to which the claim applies.

Label: Claim Diagnostic Criteria
Definition: The criteria or instruments used to establish the diagnosis.

Label: Claim Effect Size
Definition: The effect size reported for the claim.

Label: Claim P-Value
Definition: The p-value reported for the claim.

Label: Claim Population Qualifiers
Definition: Other qualifiers of the population, such as comorbidity or medication status.

Label: Claim Sample Size
Definition: The number of participants in each group the claim compares.
Example: 48 participants with ASD and 63 typically developing controls

Label: Claim Sex Distribution
Definition: The sex distribution of the participants to which the claim applies.
Example: 39 male and 9 female in the ASD group

Label: Claim Sex Group
Allowed_Values: Male Only; Female Only; Mixed; Not Specified
Definition: The sex composition of the participants to which the claim applies. It is a coarse facet used to show whether claims about the same finding come from comparable samples.

Label: Claim Survived Correction
Definition: Whether the finding remained significant after multiple-comparison correction.

Label: Claim Registration Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for values that scripts derive after extraction: the claim key and the ontology versions used for grounding.
Standards_And_Sources: Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Key
Definition: A deterministic key built from the grounded condition, region, laterality, measure and direction. Claim records with the same key are the same claim reported by different publications.

Label: Claim Key Complete
Definition: Whether every slot of the claim key was grounded. An incomplete key is never merged with another.

Label: Grounding Ontology Versions
Definition: The ontology versions used when the claim slots were grounded, so that grounding can be reproduced and re-run.

Label: Claim Slot Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the claim parsed into slots: condition, comparator, region, laterality, measure and direction. Each slot that is grounded to an ontology carries mapped, CURIE and unmappable sibling properties.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Comparator
Definition: The reference group the finding is measured against, as written in the article. It is not part of the claim key and is displayed to experts. Not Applicable for association claims.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Condition
Definition: The condition or variable of interest of the claim, exactly as written in the article. It is not normalized by the LLM.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Condition Mapped
Definition: The ontology term for the condition, found by the deterministic grounding script (MONDO, then HP).

Label: Claim Condition Mapped CURIE
Definition: The CURIE of the matched condition term, with the ontology version.

Label: Claim Condition Unmappable
Definition: The condition string that no ontology term matched. Held for curator review and contribution to InterLex.

Label: Claim Direction
Allowed_Values: Increased; Decreased; No Difference; Positive Association; Negative Association; No Association
Definition: The direction of the finding relative to the comparator, or of the association.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Laterality
Definition: The side of the brain to which the region refers.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Laterality Mapped Curie
Definition: The CURIE of the term for the side, found by the deterministic grounding script: BSPO left side or right side, and PATO bilateral. Not Specified has no term.

Label: Claim Measure
Definition: The imaging-derived measure the claim is about, exactly as written in the article.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Measure Mapped CURIE
Definition: The CURIEs of the terms matched to the measure text by the grounding script, as a JSON list with the ontology versions. The first is the PATO quality (for example volume, thickness, area). A tissue term from UBERON follows when the measure names one (for example gray matter), so gray matter volume and white matter volume stay different measures.

Label: Claim Measure Unmappable
Definition: The measure string that no PATO quality matched, for example fractional anisotropy or gyrification index. Held for curator review and contribution to InterLex.

Label: Claim Region
Definition: The brain region of the claim, exactly as written in the article, without the laterality.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Region Mapped
Definition: The ontology term for the region, found by the deterministic grounding script (UBERON).

Label: Claim Region Mapped CURIE
Definition: The CURIE of the matched region term, with the ontology version.

Label: Claim Region Unmappable
Definition: The region string that no ontology term matched. Held for curator review and contribution to InterLex.

Label: Claim Variable Type
Allowed_Values: Diagnosis; Trait or Phenotype; Exposure; Demographic; Other
Definition: The kind of variable the condition slot holds: a diagnosis, a trait or phenotype, an exposure, a demographic variable or something else.
Standards_And_Sources: Morgan RL, Whaley P, Thayer KA, Schünemann HJ. Identifying the PECO: A framework for formulating good questions to explore the association of environmental and other exposures with health outcomes. Environment International 2018;121(Pt 1):1027-1031. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2018.07.015 || Richardson WS, Wilson MC, Nishikawa J, Hayward RS. The well-built clinical question: a key to evidence-based decisions. ACP Journal Club 1995;123(3):A12-3.

Label: Claim Statement Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for what the paper says and where it says it: the atomic claim, its supporting quote and its location.
Standards_And_Sources: Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA. Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications. Journal of Biomedical Semantics 2014;5:28. doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28 || Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Evidence Level
Definition: Whether the claim was extracted from the full text or from the abstract only. Set by the registry.
Standards_And_Sources: Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA. Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications. Journal of Biomedical Semantics 2014;5:28. doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28 || Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Evidence Quote
Definition: The verbatim passage of the article that supports the claim. The pipeline rejects a claim whose quote cannot be found in the source text.
Example: Results demonstrated young children with ASD had increased gray matter volumes (GMVs) in the right medial superior frontal gyrus and left fusiform gyrus compared with the TD group.
Standards_And_Sources: Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA. Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications. Journal of Biomedical Semantics 2014;5:28. doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28 || Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Role
Definition: Whether the claim is a main claim of the article or a supporting one.

Label: Claim Source Reference
Definition: The table or figure the claim draws on, if any.
Standards_And_Sources: Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA. Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications. Journal of Biomedical Semantics 2014;5:28. doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28 || Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Source Section
Allowed_Values: Abstract; Conclusion; Discussion; Figures; Introduction; Methods; References; Results; Tables; Title
Definition: The article section from which the quote was taken.
Standards_And_Sources: Clark T, Ciccarese PN, Goble CA. Micropublications: a semantic model for claims, evidence, arguments and annotations in biomedical communications. Journal of Biomedical Semantics 2014;5:28. doi:10.1186/2041-1480-5-28 || Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Claim Statement
Definition: One atomic claim written as a single self-contained sentence: one finding about one condition, one region, one measure and one direction, against one comparator. A sentence that reports several regions yields several claims.
Example: Young children with ASD have increased gray matter volumes in the left fusiform gyrus compared with TD children.
Standards_And_Sources: Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613 || Kuhn T, Barbano PE, Nagy ML, Krauthammer M. Broadening the scope of nanopublications. In: The Semantic Web: Semantics and Big Data (ESWC 2013). Lecture Notes in Computer Science 7882:487-501. doi:10.1007/978-3-642-38288-8_33

Label: Extraction Provenance Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the versions and dates needed to reproduce an extraction run.
Standards_And_Sources: Groth P, Gibson A, Velterop J. The anatomy of a nanopublication. Information Services and Use 2010;30:51-56. doi:10.3233/ISU-2010-0613

Label: Extraction Date
Definition: The date and time of the extraction run.

Label: Extraction Model ID
Definition: The identifier of the language model that performed the extraction.

Label: Extraction Prompt Version
Definition: The version of the prompts, assembled from the ontology, used for the extraction.

Label: Ontology Version
Definition: The version of this ontology used for the extraction.

Label: Parser Version
Definition: The version of the document parser used to prepare the article text.

Label: Registry Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for facts about a publication that are known before extraction begins: file type, full-text availability, article classification and duplicate detection.

Label: Article Classification
Definition: Whether the article reports its own primary study (Primary) or synthesizes other studies, such as a review or meta-analysis (Secondary). In version 0.1 secondary articles skip study and claim extraction.

Label: Available Sections
Definition: The article sections detected in the source file, for example Abstract, Methods, Results and Tables.

Label: Content Hash
Definition: A hash of the source file, used to detect byte-identical duplicates.

Label: Document Type
Definition: Whether the source file is a native PDF with a text layer or a scanned PDF that requires OCR.

Label: Duplicate Of ID
Definition: Links a Publication to the Publication it duplicates, for example a preprint and its published version, so that both are not counted as independent confirmations.

Label: Full Text Available
Definition: Whether the full text of the article is available. Abstract-only records are processed with evidence level Abstract Only and are not sent to SciScore.

Label: SciScore Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the reporting-quality profile of a publication returned by SciScore. Populated by an API call per unique article, not by the LLM.

Label: SciScore Detected Resources
Definition: The key resources detected by SciScore, such as software and datasets, with their RRIDs, as JSON.

Label: SciScore Detected Statistical Tests
Definition: The statistical tests detected by SciScore in the Methods section.

Label: SciScore Report Date
Definition: The date of the SciScore report.

Label: SciScore Resources Subscore
Definition: The key-resources part of the SciScore.

Label: SciScore Rigor Criteria
Definition: The per-criterion rigor results of the SciScore report, as JSON.

Label: SciScore Rigor Subscore
Definition: The rigor part of the SciScore.

Label: SciScore Supporting Sentences
Definition: The Methods sentences SciScore quotes as support, as JSON.

Label: SciScore Total
Definition: The total SciScore of the article, from 0 to 10.

Label: SciScore Version
Definition: The SciScore version that produced the report.

Label: Study Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for what is reported once per study and shared by all of its claims: design, dataset, imaging, analysis and statistical methods.

Label: Analysis Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for image analysis details: software, atlas, settings and operating system.

Label: Analysis Settings
Definition: Analysis settings that affect results, such as smoothing kernel, thresholds and preprocessing choices.
Example: Smoothing kernel of 8 mm FWHM; default recon-all settings.

Label: Analysis Software
Definition: The software used to analyze the images, as named in the article.

Label: Analysis Software RRID
Definition: The RRID of the analysis software, taken from the article or the SciScore report. Derived, not extracted from free text by the LLM.

Label: Analysis Software Version
Definition: The version of the analysis software.

Label: Atlas Parcellation
Definition: The atlas or parcellation used to define brain regions.

Label: Morphometry Method
Allowed_Values: Voxel-Based Morphometry; Surface-Based Morphometry; Region-of-Interest Volumetry; Manual Tracing; Tensor-Based Morphometry; Other; Not Specified
Definition: The analysis technique used to measure brain structure, as a coarse category for filtering. The software, version and settings are recorded in their own fields. Candidate values for the NIDM-Terms vocabulary in InterLex.

Label: Operating System
Definition: The operating system on which the analysis ran.

Label: Dataset Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the dataset or cohort whose participants were studied.

Label: Study Dataset
Definition: The dataset or cohort whose participants were studied, as named in the article. Used to flag claims that share a cohort and are therefore not independent.

Label: Study Dataset RRID
Definition: The RRID of the dataset, where the article or the SciScore report gives one. Derived, not extracted from free text by the LLM.

Label: Imaging Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for image acquisition details.

Label: Image Resolution
Definition: The spatial resolution of the acquired images.

Label: Imaging Modality
Definition: The imaging modality and contrast analyzed.

Label: Imaging Modality Mapped Curie
Definition: The CURIEs of the NIDM terms matched to the imaging modality text (acquisition modality, image contrast type and image usage type), with the term set version. Found by the grounding script.

Label: Imaging Modality Unmappable
Definition: The imaging modality string that no NIDM term matched. Held for curator review and contribution to NIDM-Terms in InterLex.

Label: Magnetic Field Strength
Definition: The magnetic field strength of the scanner.

Label: Pulse Sequence
Definition: The pulse sequence and its main acquisition parameters.
Example: MPRAGE, TR 2300 ms, TE 2.98 ms, flip angle 9 degrees

Label: Scanner Manufacturer Model
Definition: The manufacturer and model of the MRI scanner.

Label: Statistical Methods Metadata
Definition: Grouping property for the statistical methods described in the Methods section.

Label: Covariates
Definition: The covariates included in the statistical model.
Example: Age, sex, site and total intracranial volume

Label: Multiple Comparison Correction
Definition: The method used to correct for multiple comparisons, with its threshold.
Example: False discovery rate correction at q < 0.05

Label: Statistical Test
Definition: The statistical test or model used for the group comparison or association.

Label: Study Design Type
Definition: The design of the study, for example case-control, longitudinal, cross-sectional or mega-analysis.
Example: Cross-sectional case-control study using voxel-based morphometry.

Label: Publication ID
Definition: A unique identifier for one Publication, generated by the registry when the article is first ingested.

Label: Reported Study ID
Definition: Links a Publication to the Study it reports.

Label: Reporting Publication ID
Definition: Links a Claim record to the Publication in which it is reported.

Label: Source Study ID
Definition: Links a Claim record to the Study whose data produced it.

Label: Study ID
Definition: A unique identifier for one Study, generated by the registry.
